title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
gist: LinkedIn replaced Argo CD for app deployments with an internal library-based GitOps engine running one ephemeral pod per deployment across 250+ Kubernetes clusters, cutting deployment-infra failures from 925 to 63 despite 3.7x more volume; it cites watch contention and managedFields truncation as architectural limits of controller-based GitOps at scale.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's custom GitOps engine deploys across over 250 Kubernetes clusters, more than 4,000 services and over 100,000 deployments per week, with clusters of up to 5,000 nodes.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.locator: In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed

insights.claim: After replacing Argo CD, LinkedIn's deployment-infrastructure failures fell from 925 to 63 despite a 3.7x increase in deployment volume, and median time to detect and conclude a failed deployment dropped from 16.1 to 2.45 minutes.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude reliability gain challenges assumptions about off-the-shelf GitOps at scale.
insights.locator: In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed

insights.claim: LinkedIn acknowledges its improvement is not solely due to the new engine, as orchestrator error classification also improved; comparisons use the same month a year apart, with May 2026 the first clean post-migration month after a July 2025–April 2026 migration, and exclude drift errors.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Headline numbers are partly confounded; treat as directional.
insights.locator: The comparison uses the same calendar

insights.claim: Median successful deployment duration is similar on both systems, but mean and tail latency improved, which LinkedIn attributes to a namespace-scoped informer cache.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Tail-latency gains matter more than medians for large fleets.
insights.locator: The comparison uses the same calendar

themes.theme: Why Argo CD broke at LinkedIn scale

insights.claim: Argo CD maintains one watch per group-version-resource across Applications, so on clusters with low resource-type diversity etcd churn from one app slows syncs for all; in one LinkedIn test sync took under 3 minutes at 60,000 pods but over 10 minutes beyond 80,000.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Shared-controller GitOps tools face nonlinear scaling limits on very large clusters.
insights.locator: Two of the issues were architectural.

insights.claim: Kubernetes truncates managedFields after more than 10 distinct field managers, so server-side-apply PATCH can lose field ownership and leave a container removed from a manifest running on the live Pod — observed in LinkedIn's multi-container AI workloads.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Silent configuration drift in AI workloads is a hidden reliability and security risk.
insights.locator: Two of the issues were architectural.

insights.claim: LinkedIn listed further Argo CD pain points: no observedGeneration to tie sync/health to a deployment, stale repo-server cache resolving to unintended revisions, fleet-wide controller restarts for CRD schema changes, spurious OutOfSync states, and buried error messages.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Catalog of operational gaps that commercial GitOps vendors could target.
insights.locator: LinkedIn started with one Argo CD

insights.claim: Maintaining 200+ Argo CD instances made each upgrade a multi-week project for LinkedIn, which still uses Argo CD for cluster add-ons and system services.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Per-cluster instance topologies carry heavy upgrade toil.

insights.claim: LinkedIn evaluated Flux but rejected it as sharing Argo CD's controller paradigm, instead building a library engine where each deployment runs in its own pod with no shared controller state, using PUT full replacements with exponential-backoff retries and a 3-way diff that fails deployments on genuine drift.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Signals an architectural shift away from shared-controller GitOps at hyperscale.

insights.claim: LinkedIn concludes that per-deployment isolation, not controller tuning, lets deployment systems scale with compute, and that build-or-extend decisions depend on the operational model.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Undercuts the 'tune the controller' path; favors ephemeral-worker architectures.
insights.locator: Teams running Argo CD at scale

insights.claim: Teams running Argo CD at scale can check field-manager counts on long-lived objects and whether sync latency tracks total pod count on shared clusters, the latter pointing to watch contention.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Low-cost diagnostics for silent failure modes before a rewrite.
insights.locator: Teams running Argo CD at scale

insights.claim: Other large operators also built custom deployment logic: Uber's Up platform uses a long-running Uber Deployment Controller per deployment, while Airbnb's kube-gen and deploy tool handled roughly 125,000 production deploys a year with atomic success/failure semantics.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Pattern: at hyperscale, firms build rather than adopt general-purpose GitOps; limits TAM for vendors at the top end.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's GitOps engine is internal with no open-source release mentioned.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: No direct competitive threat to Argo CD/Flux ecosystems yet.
